feedback: Written before this geometry has raced. Evidence: iteration 9 (y=0.045, ±0.055, base_speed 1.4) still had 0.9 line losses on s-bend and 1.0 on slalom, so curve speed is ruled out as the cause. Iteration 5 (y=0.03, ±0.05) had zero losses but s-bend progress of only 0.040. Iteration 6 (y=0.06, ±0.05) gave the best progress (s-bend 0.157) at the cost of about one loss per trial. What I had to do in the controller: I kept the iteration 9 gains and weights unchanged, so the geometry change is isolated. Span has not moved the oval floor (about 0.061) in any iteration, and body width cannot raise the 0.06 m off-track limit within range, so I do not expect the floor to move. If line losses persist at y=0.05 with ±0.06, the loss is tied to the forward row itself, and the next move is back toward y=0.03 with ±0.06. If losses clear and s-bend progress holds near 0.14, the next test is span, not row.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay at or above 0.9 on s-bend and slalom at y=0.05 with ±0.06, return the row to y=0.03 with ±0.06, because iteration 2 (y=0.03, ±0.06) had zero losses and iteration 6 to 9 showed that forward rows at 0.045 to 0.06 always lost the line.

If line losses clear at y=0.05 but slalom progress falls below about 0.10, narrow the outer sensors to x=±0.055 at y=0.05, because iteration 1 (±0.04) reached slalom progress 0.110 and iteration 9 (±0.055) held 0.100 at the forward row.

If losses are cut in half but not removed, try y=0.04 with ±0.06 as a bracket between the zero-loss row y=0.03 and the lossy row y=0.045, because iterations 5 and 9 bound the loss onset somewhere between those rows.
